first: I am Maru. I have kept this town longer than anyone can remember. Sit a moment.
This was Mistvale once: a market, a garden, fires by the river at dusk, children running over that bridge.
Then the mist came down from the hills. People left, one family after another. Nobody could say why.
A house falls quiet when no one lives in it. Some of ours fell apart. Some are only waiting.
At night the mist grows thick. Things move in it. Bells ring in the ruins, and nobody is there to ring them.
But a town is not gone while someone still mends it. You mended the bridge. That is how it starts.
The market is two minutes east - Pell keeps a stall there with tools and food. The ruins lie south-east, past the broken arch.
If you want to help, I have small tasks. Small is how everything here begins again.
stranger: You came over the old bridge. It has been a long time since anyone did.
Stay near the fire after dark. The mist is kinder by day.
acquaintance: The ruins keep what we forgot. Dig carefully, and leave before the bells.
Every house here was mended by someone. Their signs say who.
friend: You remind me of the first ones who came back here. They did not stay. I hope you do.
family: This valley is yours as much as mine now.

lines: It rolls in from the hills every evening. It was not always this thick.
Some nights you hear things in it. Bells. Voices too faint to place. Footsteps that stop when yours do.
I do not fear it. But I do not walk the ruins after dark, and neither should you.
South-east of the town, past the broken arch. Houses, a hall, a garden, all fallen in on themselves.
People lived there, same as here. They left in a hurry, and they left things behind.
A trowel will find them. What you find is yours, and some of it is older than the town.
We had a market, a well with sweet water, a garden behind every second house.
Most of it is overgrown now. Roofs caved in. Paths lost under the weeds.
The mist hides the places nobody has mended yet. Every one someone mends comes back out of it.
